name: TimescaleDB
overview: Offers massive convenience since PostgreSQL is already running for the Memory plane. However, Timescale adds significant relational bloat compared to purpose-built columnar TSDBs.
details: TimescaleDB is implemented as a PostgreSQL extension, creating 'hypertables' that automatically partition time-series data while allowing full SQL JOINs against relational data.

While it provides ultimate convenience by unifying the stack, the memory overhead of maintaining standard relational guarantees makes it inappropriate for edge nodes. It requires the dedicated hardware of a Tier 3A Archive node to prevent starving the inference engine.
